Surah al-Dukhan (The Smoke)

Its purpose is warning against destruction for those who do not accept what is in the Noble, Wise Reminder of good and blessing, a mercy He made common among all His creation. This is indicated by its name, al-Dukhan (the Smoke), when its verses are pondered, along with the clarity of what is in it and its allusions: "In the name of God" (the King, the Mighty, the One, the Subduer), "the All-Merciful" (who encompassed all with the blessing of warning), "the Most Merciful" (who [specified] the people of His love with the mercy of glad tidings).

﴿Ha, Mim﴾. The indication to some of the secrets of its sister surahs has already been mentioned.

When al-Zukhruf was concluded with a hidden glad tiding and an apparent warning, and what He, glorified is He, had given good news of, namely the knowledge of the Arabs and their safety from the calamities they were in, seemed unlikely, He opened this surah with something similar, swearing an oath upon it, and said: ﴿By the Book﴾ [i.e., the one gathering] (p-2) every good, ﴿that makes things clear﴾, i.e., clear in itself, clarifying what preceded of the subtle glad tidings to the people of purity and insight, plainly warning by explicit expression, and other than that of everything intended by it. And because of the unlikelihood mentioned, He emphasized the answer to the oath and presented it in the manner of majesty, saying:

When al-Zukhruf was concluded with a hidden glad tiding and an apparent warning, and what He, glorified is He, had given good news of, namely the knowledge of the Arabs and their safety from the calamities they were in, seemed unlikely, He opened this surah with something similar, swearing an oath upon it, and said: ﴿By the Book﴾ [i.e., the one gathering] (p-2) every good, ﴿that makes things clear﴾, i.e., clear in itself, clarifying what preceded of the subtle glad tidings to the people of purity and insight, plainly warning by explicit expression, and other than that of everything intended by it. And because of the unlikelihood mentioned, He emphasized the answer to the oath and presented it in the manner of majesty, saying:

﴿Indeed﴾, meaning: by the majesty We possess, ﴿We sent it down﴾, that is, the Book, either all at once to the House of Honour (Bayt al-'Izzah) in the lowest heaven, or We began sending it down to the earth ﴿on a blessed night﴾, that is, the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), as said by Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them. Or it is the middle of Sha'ban, and therefore there proceed from it effects of influence in religion and in worldly life that understanding cannot encompass. Al-Ustadh Abu al-Qasim al-Qushayri said: It descends to the lowest heaven every year in the measure that Jibril, peace be upon him, used to bring down to the Messenger (ﷺ) in that year. He named it ﴿blessed﴾ because it is the night of the opening of union, and the most blessed of nights, in which the servant is present with his heart, witnessing his Lord, enjoying the lights of union and finding the breeze of nearness. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': The greatest of nights in blessing is the one in which the realities of things are unveiled.

Since this clarifies what the end of that passage hinted at, in the outward form of warning, of good tidings, he gave the reason for the sending down, or began anew with what contains clear warning, leading to the meanings that call for good tidings. So He said, emphasising in order to refute their denial: ﴿Indeed﴾, meaning: according to what We are upon of majesty, ﴿We have always been﴾, by the majesty We possess, ﴿warners﴾ to Our servants. We do not seize them without warning. Therefore, out of Our mercy towards these people, who are the most tender of people in nature, the purest of hearts and the most retentive of hearing, We bring them, by what We have prepared them with, to a station that no one else reaches and that none of the other lofty qualities of character, dispositions and acquisition of all virtues comes close to.

Imam Abu Ja'far Ibn al-Zubayr said: Since the surah of Ha-Mim al-Sajdah and the surah of al-Shura contained mention of the Glorious Book to the extent that has been indicated, which surah Ghafir does not include any of, and from the totality of that there resulted the information about its being sent down from Allah and its being detailed, and its being an Arabic Qur'an, up to what He, exalted is He, mentioned of its characteristics, up to His saying: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned﴾ (Az-Zukhruf 43:44), and the speech after this connected, part to part, up to the end of the surah, He, exalted is He, opened Surat al-Dukhan with what completes that purpose, which is the definition of the time of its sending down to (p-4) the lowest heaven. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed We sent it down on a blessed night﴾, then He mentioned its excellence, saying: ﴿therein every wise matter is distinguished﴾ (Al-Dukhan 44:4). Thus there resulted the description of the Book with its characteristics and the definition of the time of its sending down to the lowest heaven. The most important of that was presented in the two surahs before, and the definition of the time of its sending down to the lowest heaven was delayed, since it is not in the emphasis like the preceding. Then right after this came a detailed threat that had been summarised in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So turn away from them and say, "Peace," for they will come to know﴾ (Az-Zukhruf 43:89), and what preceded it of His saying: ﴿Or have they determined a matter, then indeed We are determined﴾ (Az-Zukhruf 43:79), and His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private talk?﴾ (Az-Zukhruf 43:80), and His declaring Himself, glorified and exalted is He, free of the great slander of their attributing to Him partners and offspring, up to the end of the surah. So He detailed some of what those verses had summarised in His saying, exalted is He, at the beginning of Surat al-Dukhan: ﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾ (Al-Dukhan 44:10), and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The day We will strike the greatest assault﴾ (Al-Dukhan 44:16), indicating the day of Badr. Then He mentioned the matter of others besides them in this and their destruction for the evil they committed, so that they would perceive that there is no escape for them if they had sense and took warning. Then He alluded to their chief in his saying: "Is not the dominion of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Are you not then seeing?" (Az-Zukhruf 43:51), and his saying: "Between its two lava-fields there is none more honourable or nobler than me." Then He, exalted is He, mentioned: (p-5) ﴿the tree of Zaqqum﴾ (As-Saffat 37:62), up to His saying: ﴿Taste, indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾ (Al-Dukhan 44:49). All of this was joined together in a way that dazzles the minds. Then it was followed by mention of the state of the God-fearing, in keeping with the regular pattern of paired encouragement and warning, in order to make clear the state of both groups and so that knowledge of the clear path from the two paths would result. Then He said to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿So We have only made it easy in your tongue, that perhaps they will remember﴾ (Al-Dukhan 44:58), and He informed him, along with clarifying the matter and making it evident, that: ﴿He who fears will be reminded﴾ (Al-A'la 87:10). Then He said: ﴿So watch﴾ (Al-Dukhan 44:10), your promise and their threat, ﴿indeed they are watching﴾ (Al-Dukhan 44:59).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 4:

When he described the night of the sending down of this Qur'an as blessed, and informed that among the greatest of its blessings is warning (al-nidhara), and warning, although it is distinguished from good tidings (al-bishara), is a great matter that necessitates the distinguishing (furqan) between good and bad deeds, leading to every good, as evidenced by the fact that the followers of the people of blessing among the scholars, when the command of the scholar and the command of the oppressor conflict in their view, they give precedence to the command of the oppressor because they fear his warning, and they neglect the command of the scholar, even though the hope in his good tidings is great, he said, giving the reason for its blessing after giving the reason for the sending down within it, and generalizing it to include what is attained within it of the blessings of excellence: ﴿Therein﴾, i.e., in the blessed night, whether we say it is the Night of Power (laylat al-qadr) or the Night of the Middle (laylat al-nisf), essentially or ultimately, ﴿is made distinct﴾, i.e., is spread out, explained, detailed and clarified time after time, ﴿every wise affair﴾, i.e., a matter made firm, which cannot be impugned in any respect, from all that is revealed of books and other things, and provisions, and terms of life, and victory and defeat, and fertility and drought, and other than these, from all categories of events, and in detail as to their times and places. And this is made known to the angels from that night until its like in the coming year, so they find it the same, and thereby their faith increases.

Al-Baghawi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: It is written from the Mother of the Book [in the Night of Power] what will occur in the year of good and evil, and of provisions and terms of life. He said: Abu al-Duha narrated from him that Allah, exalted is He, decrees the decrees on the night of the middle of Sha'ban, then hands them over to their owners on the Night of Power. And al-Kirmani said: He hands them over to their owners and their agents among the angels on the night of the twenty-seventh of the month of Ramadan.

When this (the Qur'an) implies matters without limit, He (exalted is He) made clear that there is no burden upon Him in it, and no renewal with Him at any time of anything that did not exist before, other than the connection of power to what accords with His will. So He said, emphasizing the magnificence of what its description as "wise" includes: ﴿a command﴾, meaning: with all of this, in its spread and its lack of confinement, is a single, very great command, without plurality in it, which We arranged in pre-eternity, determined, perfected, and chose, so that it would come into being at its times by measure, and be brought forth in accordance with its (p-7) firmness in its appointed times, in less than the blink of an eye. And He indicated that He is not overwhelmed by what is under His power (exalted is He), by affirming the preposition, so He said: ﴿from Us﴾, meaning: from the extraordinary events, the marvels, and what lies beyond them. When He had made clear the state of the Criterion (al-Furqan), of which warning is a part, He gave its reason with His words, emphasizing it against their denial: ﴿Indeed We﴾, meaning: with what belongs to Us of the attributes of perfection and the perfection of greatness, ﴿were﴾, meaning: from eternity to eternity, ﴿senders﴾, meaning: for Us is the attribute of sending, with the capacity to do so at every time. Sending is for the benefit of the servants, and it necessarily involves the Criterion, through good tidings, warning, and other things, so that there will be no confusion, and so that no one has any proof against God after the messengers. This coherent discourse and this closely joined speech, whose parts are arranged in the finest order, in describing the Night of Revelation, indicates that no scroll or book was sent down except in this night. It therefore indicates that it is the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), on account of the reports stating that all the books were sent down in it, as I have explained in my book *Masa'id al-Nazar li'l-Ishraf 'ala Maqasid al-Suwar* (The Ascents of Contemplation for Overseeing the Aims of the Surahs). Likewise is His saying in the surah of al-Qadr: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord, with every command﴾ [al-Qadr: 4]. For the revelation, which [is] the collection of all that, is the spirit of the wise matters. And He (exalted is He) made clear the state of the messages (p-8) with His words:

Mercy. This is also an act of justice, required by the use of the word "mercy" in place of the style of speaking in the first person of majesty found in His words "from Us" through to His words: ﴿from your Lord﴾, meaning: the One who has done good to you by sending you and sending every prophet who passed before you. Their messages were for spreading lights among the servants and laying the groundwork of the laws among the servants, until hearts were illuminated and souls found peace, through what they came to recognize of the legislation of laws and the preparation of religions. Thus the ways of the Lord were made easy for the generalization of your message, until your lights filled the horizons, so you became the culmination of all who preceded you among the companions.

Since a message necessarily involves hearing and knowledge, He said: ﴿Indeed He is﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿the All-Hearing﴾, that is, He is the Living, the Willing, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾, that is, He is the Powerful, the All-Seeing, the Speaking. He hears what His messengers say and what is said to them, and everything that can be heard, even if it is of a kind that no one else hears, such as inner speech and other things. This relates to our hearing as the relation of what you hear of speech to the hearing of a deaf person; His hearing is not like our hearing. Rather, it relates to things heard as they are before they come into existence, just as His knowledge relates to things known as they are before they come into being.

[p. 9] When He mentioned the sending down of the Book in that most blessed state, for the sake of sending the Messenger, and explained that the greatest fruit of the sending is warning, because of what the addressees have from themselves (p. 9) of the Torah, He indicated this through the firm arrangement that the wisdom of nurturing requires, and said: ﴿Lord﴾, meaning the Owner, Originator and Manager of ﴿the heavens﴾, meaning all the celestial bodies, and ﴿the earth﴾ and what is in it, and ﴿whatever is between them﴾, of what you observe of this expanse and what is in it of air and other things, of what you know of the acquisitions of the servants, and of other things you do not know. It is known that He is the Lord of the Throne (al-'Arsh) and the Footstool (al-Kursi). Thus it is known from this that He is the Owner of the whole dominion.

Since they acknowledged this lordship, and they would be too proud to be described as not verifying anything they acknowledge, He pointed to what this acknowledgment necessitates for them, if they are, as they claim, [of] verification, and so He said: ﴿if you are certain﴾, meaning: if you have certainty that He is the Creator of what He has fixed in your natures and dispositions, the firm knowledge pure and free of the impurities of turbidity, from the shares of the souls and the obstacles of attachments. Then you know that these very dense bodies, some of which are elevated above others, must have a holder that you observe, while each of them undergoes changes of various kinds, from a Lord, and that they would not be in this order except that He is (p. 10) perfect in knowledge, all-encompassing in power, free in His management, and wise in all His affairs and all His decrees. And that it is not permissible in wisdom that He leave those in them of the wise intelligent beings, who are the essence of what is in them both, as something neglected, where some of them transgress against others, without a messenger informing them of His commands, His rulings and His prohibitions, alerting them that He created this whole creation only for their sake, so that they would beware of His punishment and bind themselves through gratitude for the various kinds of gifts He has bestowed upon them.

When this clear reflection established His lordship (*rububiyyah*), and the unbroken management (*tadbir*) of affairs over a long period established His oneness (*wahdaniyyah*), and the universe does not run on a single system in every respect, which shows He acted by choice and by His power, He stated this explicitly, alerting them that correct reflection necessarily produced it. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿There is no god but Him﴾ [i.e., for otherwise one of them would have contested Him in their affair, or some part of it would have contested Him, or it would have been possible for someone to contest Him, in which case He would necessarily be in need. And otherwise, whoever could be removed from Him and opposed Him would have repelled Him, so He would not be fit to govern and subdue everyone who opposes His messengers, or to inspire everyone who agrees with them, over the passing of time, the lengthening of the ages, and the extension of events, in a continuous system and a firm, stable state].

[p. 11] When it was established that He alone is the One who bestows and withdraws, and withdrawal is the stronger proof of dominance, He reminded them of what they have of this within themselves, saying, glorified is He: ﴿Your Lord﴾ [i.e., the One who bestowed upon you what you witness of blessings in spirits and other things] ﴿and the Lord of your forefathers﴾. Since they witnessed His lordship over their nearest forefathers just as they witness it for themselves, He raised their gaze to the ultimate, saying: ﴿the earliest ones﴾ [i.e., those upon whom He bestowed what He bestowed upon you, then took it from them, as you know. So none of them was able to resist, nor to hope to contest it by any means of defense].

Since most of them deny what they were obliged to affirm with this shining proof and manifest, dominating authority, out of obstinacy and contentiousness, even though inwardly they are otherwise, their act became the act of the doubter who plays. The intended meaning, in view of what appears of their condition, is: "But you are not certain of any knowledge at all." He builds on this his saying, together with the turn to the third person, as a turning away from them, signaling anger, and that they are deserving of being hastened to ruin: ﴿Rather they﴾, that is, in their inner selves, ﴿are in doubt﴾, because they do not strip their souls of the impurities of what clouds them, for the clarity of knowledge. Then he informed his Prophet ﷺ that what occupies them from this important matter is the state of children, while they claim perfection with the characteristics of the noble men. So He said: ﴿they play﴾, that is, they constantly act like one who has abandoned what he is in, of the utmost seriousness about which there is no doubt, for the play that has no benefit and no fruit whatsoever for them, after the act of the doubter in turning away and not hastening to belief and acceptance.

When this was the place where the Messenger ﷺ might say what is understood from the context, "What did he do with them after this clear statement, which left no ambiguity for anyone?", He made the following a consequence of that, as consolation to him and as a threat to them: ﴿So watch for them﴾, that is, wait with all your effort, rising above them, observing their conditions like one who is a guard over them, protecting yourself from their like with a resolve like that of the lion with the sharp gaze (al-asad al-arqab). The verb is transitive, but it has been made intransitive to inspire awe, so that the mind goes in every direction regarding its object. The original meaning is probably what results from the causes of your victory and the requirements of their humiliation. ﴿The day the sky brings forth﴾, that is, as it appears to the eye, because of what covers the sight from the severe hardship of hunger, if what is meant is the famine that they suffered, arising from the drought that was caused by his ﷺ saying: "O Allah, support me against them with seven years like the seven years of Joseph." It is narrated in the Sahih that a man among them would see between the sky and the earth something like smoke. In reality, what is meant is at the approach of the Hour and immediately after its establishment, for it is reported that it will come at that time and cover the people, and that the believer will experience from it something like a cold in the head. It is also possible that what is meant is more general than all of that, and its beginning is the time of the drought [and it was a sign of what follows it, or from it is what comes when the smoke emerges from the drought] that occurs before it or otherwise, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have hidden for you a hidden thing; what is it?" He said: "The smoke (al-dukh)." So it was explained as smoke. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿with manifest smoke﴾, that is, clear, with no ambiguity in it for the one who sees it, and making clear other signs to the discerning.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 11:

(p-14) ﴿Covering the people﴾, i.e., those threatened by this, namely those who were content with the lowest point of wavering and turbulence instead of the summit of steadfastness in the rank of rightness. Muslim related in his Sahih from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Hasten to good deeds before six: the Dajjal (the false messiah), the smoke, the beast of the earth, the rising of the sun from its west, the matter of the common people (al-'amma), and the special concern of each one of you (khuwaysat ahadikum)."

Since it is well known that when it comes, they will say, following the custom of their ignorance: "What is this?" they were answered with His words, the Exalted, as a report from the language of the state, or the statement of some of them or of some of the friends of Allah: ﴿This is a painful punishment﴾, whose pain reaches the heart and goes to the extreme of its agony, because of what you used to cause pain to your callers to Allah by rejecting their words and mocking them, and because of your deception by the abundance of number [and strength] and reinforcement.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 12:

Since it is as if it were said: "What did they say when they became certain of that?" It is said: They said, while the bonds of those resolutions had come undone, and those powers had weakened in every resolute person, and those lofty aspirations had fallen down after their height, claiming that they were, in their utmost submission, among the people of nearness and good pleasure: ﴿Our Lord﴾, that is, O Originator for us and Benefactor to us, ﴿remove from us the punishment﴾. Then they gave as the reason for this what they knew to be the cause that requires its removal, so they said, emphasizing it in response to the contradiction between their state and their former report: ﴿Indeed, we are believers﴾, that is, deeply immersed in the attribute of faith and arrived at the rank of certainty. This may be taken to mean after the sun rises from its west. Al-Shaykhan related from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not come until the sun rises from its west. When it rises and people see it, they will all believe, and that is the time when faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before," then he recited the verse. And if what is meant by the punishment is the drought that occurred, then this faith would be in the manner of a promise.

When the unveiling of the signs and the manifestation of the punishment would not add anything to the indication of the truth beyond what the Messenger ﷺ had already conveyed through the miracles he established—indeed, the Messenger's indication is greater—he was answered, as if someone had asked about their condition at that time, by a statement turning away from addressing them, as a notice of the continuance of their affliction, lest it be thought that he removed the punishment from them only because he suspected they were truthful:

﴿Annā﴾ meaning: how, and from where, ﴿lahumu al-dhikrā﴾ meaning: this great remembrance by which they described themselves ﴿wa-qad﴾ meaning: while the state is that indeed ﴿jā'ahum﴾ [there had come to them] something greater than that, with what cannot be compared ﴿rasūlun mubīn﴾ meaning: manifest to the utmost degree that he is Our messenger, and made clear to the utmost degree regarding what he brought from Us, through the signs that were displayed, and other indications besides them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 14:

Since turning away from him, together with the greatness he possesses through clear proof, was a sign of contempt for him and for those who came after him, he indicated this by the particle of delay, saying: ﴿Then﴾, that is: after what he has of lofty rank in himself and in relation to the One who sent him. Since the original human natures (al-fitar al-ula) call toward turning to the truth, inclined toward cutting oneself off to God, devoting oneself to His threshold, and seeking refuge at His side, except with an effort of the self in aversion and in treating the calls to ruin (thubur), he indicated this by expressing it with the form of tafa'ul, saying: ﴿they turned away from him﴾, that is: they obeyed what called them to turn their backs on him from the calls of desire and the impulses of appetites and personal interests. ﴿And they said﴾, that is: in addition to their wrongdoing by turning away: ﴿taught (mu'allam)﴾, that is: he was taught by someone else among mankind, ﴿a madman (majnun)﴾. So they did not mind the clear contradiction in the matter. This indicates that whoever does not care for his own honor and has no shame, there is no cure for his disease, because there is no existence of his remedy; and that if he is touched by what softens him, turns him back, and humiliates him, one cannot be sure of his returning to the bad state when that harm is lifted from him. (p-17)

Then, after He turned the address away from them as a humiliation to them, He (glory be to Him) made clear that the cause of it was that their disease is incurable, so there is never any removal of it. So He said, emphasizing it to counter their doubt that what they were in would be removed: ﴿Indeed We﴾, that is, with the greatness We possess through all-encompassing knowledge and otherwise, ﴿are removers of the punishment﴾ [that is], from you, through the supplication of your Messenger (ﷺ), ﴿a little﴾, [in order] to establish the proof against you, not because what is in your inner selves is hidden from Us. Since they had emphasized their report of belief, which is false, He (glory be to Him), who is more truthful in speech than anyone, emphasized the report of their lying, so He said, in confirmation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28] ﴿and indeed they are liars﴾ [al-An'am: 28]. ﴿Indeed you will return﴾, that is, your return to disbelief after Our removal of the punishment from you in that short time is certain, even if you emphatically affirm the attainment of belief [with strong oaths], because of the crookedness in your natures and your inclination by temperament to rush into error. So this belief of yours, which you reported as firmly established, is a passing accident and a false illusion. And if this is at the end of time, it is no wonder that the address to them is in its literal sense, whether by a king or otherwise, from among those whom God Most High returns, because that is a time of breaking customary practices and overturning regularities, in order to establish the proof against them, and to Him belongs the conclusive proof, and as a discipline (p-18) and instruction for us.

Since "the day" can refer to a gathered period under one ruling, and the time of the smoke (if it means the famine that preceded the Day of Badr, or what approaches the Hour) is called one day because of the unity of that ruling, He replaced "the Day of the Smoke" with His saying, threatening with the splitting of hearts: ﴿On the day We seize﴾, i.e., with what We possess of majesty and might, the seizing with force: ﴿the greatest seizure﴾ [i.e.,] that by which their bonds are loosened, by which their resolves and their powers are sifted, which their realities and their aspirations cannot bear, whether the seizing was on the Day of Badr or otherwise. There, whoever the test has exposed in his transgression and his rebellion against his Lord and his disobedience will be lost. It is permissible that this be a time-adverbial for ﴿will return﴾. And since His, glory be to Him, forbearance and prolonged respite was causing the dull and coarse people to doubt His threat, He said, emphasizing: ﴿Indeed, We are Avengers﴾, i.e., that is an established attribute; We have never ceased doing it to Our enemies, so that We may gladden their opposites among Our friends.

The reasoning (taqdir) was: "We certainly tested them by sending you to them, so that this would reveal to one who knows a thing only after it occurs what We have known from eternity and what has always been and never ceases to be [p. 19] of the inner states of their affairs, and so that the proof would be established against whoever opposed Us, according to your customary practice." He linked to this, warning Quraysh and consoling the Prophet ﷺ, with His words: ﴿Indeed We tested﴾, meaning: We acted, with the greatness that belongs to Us, the act of one who tests (fātin), that is, the one who examines and wishes to know the reality of a thing through granting respite (imlā') and empowerment (tamkīn), and then through sending (irsāl).

Since it is well known that the people of Pharaoh did not span the whole period of time, nor were they the nearest people in time to Quraysh, he removed the prepositional phrase (al-jārr) from before the adverbial of time (al-ẓarf) to avoid ambiguity. Alternatively, he magnified their trial because of the greatness and power they possessed, so He made it, for that reason, as though it encompassed all of time. Thus He said: ﴿before them﴾, meaning: before these Arabs, so that what has passed of their history would be a lesson (ʿibrah) and an admonition for them.

Since Pharaoh was among the most powerful of those to whom a messenger came before them, with his soldiers, wealth and power, and since the messenger who came to him had been granted, by the Prophet ﷺ, the signs (āyāt) that included control over the four elements, there were among them water, earth, fire and air. Whenever a sign came to them they would say: "O sorcerer! Call upon your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you; indeed we will be guided." [p. 20] When that was lifted from them, they returned to what they had been upon, as God, exalted is He, related about these people when the smoke came, and other things in which they resembled them, among the secrets which this arena (al-miḍmār) revealed. The end of all that was that He destroyed them all. Thus they were the clearest example of His words, exalted is He, in the preceding verse: ﴿So We destroyed those who were stronger than them in might﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 8]. He singled them out for mention from among those previously tested, saying: ﴿the people of Pharaoh﴾, meaning: together with Pharaoh, because what was a trial for his people was a trial for him as well, since the great person is more deeply rooted in the trial through what the world surrounds him with. The explicit statement of this will come at the end of the story. ﴿And there came to them﴾, that is, to those who were joined and to the one joined to them, in increase of their trial, ﴿a noble messenger﴾, meaning: they knew his nobility of lineage, character and deeds. Then he increased the explanation of his nobility by what God manifested through him of His care, by supporting him with miracles (muʿjizāt).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 18:

When he had informed them of his coming to them with the message, which can only be conveyed by speech, he explained what had reached them of it with his saying: ﴿Deliver to me the servants of Allah﴾, that is: convey [them] to me, with humility and good disposition of soul. He expressed this in the form of a command, whose disobedience is not permissible. And since between Moses, upon him be prayers and peace, and his dealings with his people there was a thick barrier of the oppression of Pharaoh and his people, he indicated it by the particle of ending (ilā, "to") and said: ﴿to me﴾, and he alerted them to the fact that he had no authority over them with his saying: ﴿the servants of Allah﴾, that is, the Children of Israel whom you have enslaved unjustly, and there is no servitude upon them except to the One who manifested in their affairs the attributes of His majesty and beauty by what He did with their forefathers, Abraham, upon him be prayers and peace, and those after him, and what will become manifest of what you see and what will happen after you.

And since they stood to gain from him, if they followed what had come to them with him, and to be harmed, if they rejected it, what is not the case for others, and since none of the people of the earth could deliver the Children of Israel to him except them, because they held power over them, the placing of the prepositional phrase in its most judicious position was appropriate. Therefore he said, emphasizing, against their denial of his message, upon him be prayers and peace: ﴿Indeed I am to you﴾, that is, specifically, by virtue of this, ﴿a messenger﴾, that is, [from] the side of the One from whom the complete message can only come. And since a person does not entrust the management of affairs except to a sufficiently trustworthy one, he said, describing himself with what removes their excuse and establishes the proof against them: ﴿trustworthy﴾, that is, one who has reached the utmost in trustworthiness, because the Sovereign, the Judge, sends only one who is like this.

ولَمّا كانَ اسْتِعْبادُ عَبْدِ الغَيْرِ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ في صُورَةِ العُلُوِّ عَلى مالِكِ العَبْدِ قالَ: ﴿وأنْ لا تَعْلُوا﴾

When the enslaving of another's servant without right takes the form of exalting oneself over the servant's owner, He said: ﴿And that you not exalt yourselves﴾, meaning: do not act with your enslaving of the Children of Israel, the Prophet of Allah and son of the Friend of Allah, in the manner of one who is haughty ﴿over Allah﴾, Who possesses the totality of greatness and the foundations of might, through the executing of His word and all the attributes of perfection. For if you do that, He will seize you with His might and destroy you with His greatness.

When the exaltation of one who disposes of a servant over the servant's owner is not established except after establishing that He owns him and does not wish that he be disposed of, He gave the reason for that in His words, emphasizing it because what he brought was about to be denied, since turning away from what has settled in the soul and been familiar for a long time is difficult: ﴿Indeed, I am coming to you﴾, and it may be either a noun of agency or a present-tense verb. And since their act was the act of one who exalts himself through authority, He said: ﴿with a authority﴾, meaning: a manifest, overpowering command from their Master, such that no one may rightly exalt himself over it, let alone exalt himself over one who is under His command, ﴿clear﴾, meaning: evident in its own sovereignty and making that sovereignty manifest to others.

Since it is one of the marvels that he killed a man from among them, then went out fleeing from them, then came back to them, especially coming to them in a manner in which he would overpower them in a great matter, without anything occurring between them and him that would erase what had passed from him, he alerted them to his coming in this state as another sign indicating the authority (al-sultan). So he said, emphasizing it as a denial of their assumption that he was in their grip: ﴿And indeed I have sought refuge﴾, i.e., I have held fast and taken shelter, ﴿in my Lord﴾, who nurtured me (rabbani) according to what His gentleness toward me and His kindness to me required, ﴿and your Lord﴾, who protected me from your killing me, by you, according to what His wisdom called for regarding your arrogance, your haughtiness, and the strength of your power, ﴿lest you stone me﴾, i.e., lest there occur at any time a killing by you of me. I did not come to you until I had secured confirmation from my Lord in this matter, for I had said: ﴿So I fear that they will kill me﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 14], and He said: ﴿We will strengthen your arm through your brother and give you both authority, so they will not reach you by Our signs﴾ [al-Qasas: 35]. So it is among My greatest signs that you will not reach me, despite your strength and your numbers, with killing, while I have no strength except through Allah, who sent me.

Given that the implied meaning was: "If you believe in this and submit to me, you will prosper," he followed it with his words: ﴿And if you do not believe me﴾, i.e., do not affirm what I have told you for my sake, ﴿then leave me alone (fa'tazilun)﴾, i.e., and if you do not leave me alone, you will be destroyed. You will not be able to kill me in any way, while I am one of those whom you subject to a terrible torment, and you slew their sons only because of me. So my Lord protected me from the one whose land was constricted for him because of me and who shed blood on my account, and Allah prevented him from reaching me with any harm before I sought refuge in Him. How much more so after He sent me and I took refuge in Him, so He gave me refuge, and I sought protection in Him, so He granted me protection.

Since the sense was: they did not believe in him, nor did they follow him, nor did they withdraw from him; rather, they plotted evil against him and sought to bring upon him calamities and disasters. But they were unable to accomplish that, and they harmed his people, and the trial grew long. This is the cause of His saying: ﴿So he called upon his Lord﴾, the One who had shown him kindness and guaranteed him his governance and the governance of his people. Then he explained what he called upon Him for by His saying: ﴿that these are a people﴾ [i.e., the contemptible, the base, the abased] ﴿who are criminals﴾, i.e., they have the power to carry out what they are attempting, ﴿criminals﴾, i.e., they are extreme in severing what I was commanded to be joined, and this entails joining what I was commanded to be severed. So the meaning was: he called upon Him with this content, and for this reason he used "an" (that), which indicates the verbal noun (maṣdariyyah).

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 23:**

Since he was one whose supplication Allah answers and whose call He honours, Allah made the following command a consequence of that: ﴿So set out by night﴾, meaning: We said to him, "Travel for most of the night." This is according to the recitation (qira'a, a canonical variant reading) of the people of Medina and Ibn Kathir, who read it with a connecting hamza (wasl), i.e. *fa-asri* with the hamza elided. According to the reading of the others, it is with a cut hamza (qat'), i.e. *fa-ash-ri* (*af'ir*). The meaning is: carry out the *sura*, which is travelling for most of the night, ﴿with My servants﴾, who are worthy of being attributed to My presence, namely your people, whom We sent you to make happy by rescuing them from those who wrong them, and by freeing them for My worship (p-25) and not for the worship of anyone other than Me.

Since Allah, glorified is He, had instructed the Children of Israel beforehand to be prepared on the night in which He commanded the journey, such that none of them would have any impediment at all, as has been explained earlier in al-A'raf from the Torah, He clarified His emphasis on this with His words ﴿by night﴾. This became an emphasis without the wording. He commanded travel at night only because the Copts had been struck with the death of their firstborn at night. So Pharaoh commanded Moses, peace be upon him, to leave with his people during that time, out of fear that the Copts would die.

When Allah, exalted is He, knew that if they delayed until dawn arrived and the death lifted from them, they would be prevented from leaving, and that if they delayed until the end of the night they would be overtaken by the Copts before reaching the sea and the Copts would kill them, He gave the reason for this command [with His words], emphasising it, because the state of the Copts when they commanded them to leave was that of one who does not believe it. He repeated in His words ﴿Indeed, you will be pursued﴾, meaning: you will be sought by your enemy with the utmost desire and effort. So do not be deceived by what they are in when commanding you to leave, of anguish over your staying among them, and their asking you to depart from them because of the spread of death among them. For hearts are in the hand of Allah, and He hardens the heart of Pharaoh (p-26) after seeing these signs, when the death lifts from them and they finish burying their dead. Then he will pursue you for what I had planned from eternity regarding your management, by drowning them all, so that My glory may appear thereby and I may repel from you the terror of their confrontation. For I know that you have no strength and no ability against them, so I did not burden you with engaging in any part of their affair.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 24:

When He had commanded him to travel by night and gave the reason for it, He commanded him regarding what he should do there and gave the reason, saying: ﴿And leave the sea [parted]﴾, meaning: when you have traveled by night with them and the enemy pursues you and you reach it, and We have commanded you to strike it so that it opens up for you to enter, and you entered and were saved, ﴿at rest﴾ after your complete exit from it; that is, spread out, wide and still, such that what is raised of its water remains raised and what is lowered remains lowered, like a wall. And the path by which you travelled will be dry, easy to traverse in the state in which you entered it, so that your enemy will enter it, and so We will be glorified by their drowning, as We promised you. Al-Baghawi said: "rahwan" means "ra-hiyan," that is, having calm (rahw), so it is named by the verbal noun. He attributed this to Muqatil. End.

Since these were the means by which the household of Pharaoh would enter it, He gave the reason for what would result from them, to calm their hearts regarding leaving the sea as an open path that the enemy would enter. So He said, emphasizing to remove the Children of Israel's doubt about the content of the report, because it is among the breaches of customary norms, along with the awe that Pharaoh and his household held in their hearts, which would make them deem it unlikely that they all would be destroyed: ﴿Indeed they are an army destined to drown﴾, that is: they are firmly established in this description, even though they possess the attribute of power and gathering, the root of which is valor, which produces superiority in affairs.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 25:

When the context, necessarily, guided toward the supposition: "So Musa set out with the servants of Allah as Allah had commanded him, and the people of Pharaoh followed them, as Allah, glorified is He, had reported; then Allah split the sea by His overpowering might and held back its water like walls by His dominating majesty, and left it, after their emerging from it, in its state. Then the servants of Satan followed them, by what had overflowed upon them of His wretchedness, so Allah drowned them by His might, and not one of them escaped," He, glorified is He, expressed all of this by His saying, in the manner of a resumptive statement: ﴿How many they left behind﴾, i.e., those whose drowning had already been decreed, so they drowned, ﴿of gardens﴾, i.e., orchards that are at the utmost of what can be of the goodness of land, the abundance of trees, the purity of fruits and plants, and their beauty which gladdens the troubled and conceals cares, and [by His saying] ﴿and springs﴾ he indicated the generosity of the land.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 26:

﴿And crops﴾, i.e., of what is below the trees. And since that is not complete except with dwellings and vistas in the gardens and other than them, He said: ﴿and a noble station﴾, i.e., a noble assembly, one worthy of a person residing therein, because the ultimate in what pleases him [is there].

(p-28) Since that [kind of thing] may come about through the toil of its owner in it, this indicates that it was through the drudgery of others while they themselves were in the utmost luxury. And this is what moved them to follow the one who used to provide all that for them, until it led them to drowning. He said: ﴿And luxury﴾. The word na'ma, with a fatha on the nun (نَعْمَة), is a noun for enjoyment, meaning affluence and a soft, abundant life. As for the one with a kasra (نِعْمَة), it is the act of bestowing favour. ﴿In which they used to be﴾, i.e., constantly, ﴿delighting themselves﴾ (fakihin), i.e., their conduct in their living was the conduct of one enjoying affluence, not the conduct of one who is compelled to sustain himself.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 28:

Since this was a matter so great that it is hardly believed to belong to anyone, he indicated its greatness and its being attained by them by his saying: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning: the matter is as We have told you, regarding their being given ease, their being brought out, their being drowned, and that they left behind all that they had been in, none of which availed them anything. So let no one be deceived by what We have tested him with of blessings, lest he be dealt with by destruction the way We dealt with them. And since the structure of the speech thus conveys the drowning of all of them, he added clarity to it by expressing it with inheritance, whose reality is taking from the deceased in an undisputed manner, so he said, conjoining it to what was previously estimated after the demonstrative: ﴿And We made it an inheritance﴾, meaning: those great affairs, ﴿to a people﴾, meaning: people (p-29) possessing strength in carrying out what they attempt, and he confirmed that they were others, as a confirmation of their drowning, by his saying: ﴿other﴾. Ibn Burjan said, and in Surat al-Shu'ara' (the verse about the Day of the Shade) he said: "and springs and treasures" in place of "and crops," since what is customary of crops is harvesting within a short period, he made them inherit their crops, their gardens, and what was in them of a noble station, a people other than the family of Pharaoh, for they were destroyed, nor the Children of Israel, for they had crossed the sea. When their rule became firmly established in the Holy Land, it connected to Egypt, so they inherited the land with its treasures, its wealth, its bounty, and its noble station. End.

When destruction necessarily brings grief for those destroyed, even if only from some of the people, and especially when they are a group, then how much more so when they are the people of a kingdom, and especially when they are at the pinnacle of leadership, He informed that they were, because of their insignificance before Him, the Exalted and Majestic, in the opposite state. Therefore He linked to what has passed His saying: ﴿So the sky and the earth did not weep over them﴾. This is a metaphor (isti'ara) for the lack of concern for them because of their insignificance. If the dwelling place does not weep, then what of the one who dwells in it, which is part of it? Abu Ya'la related in his Musnad, and al-Tirmidhi in his Jami' (and he said: "gharib"), while al-Rabadhi and al-Raqashi are weak in hadith (p-30), from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "There is no Muslim except that he has two doors in the sky: a door through which his deed ascends, and a door through which his provision descends. When he dies, they both weep over him." And he recited this verse. 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "When the believer dies, his place of prayer on earth weeps, and the channel of his deed from the sky weeps."

Since it is customary that an enemy may grant his adversary a delay at certain times, for such things as a bequest or the fulfilment of a need, and so he grants it, He informed, as a completion of the lack of concern for them, that they were below that level. So He said: ﴿Nor were they given respite﴾. And since this was a report about them after their passing, whose purpose was only to warn those who come after them, He did not mention a restriction to that time with "by His permission" or similar phrases, indicating that the long respite they had was as though it had never been, because of the magnitude of this seizing. This is unlike what passed in al-Hijr regarding the warning of the sending down of angels upon them, for the restriction of the non-granting of respite to that time serves to turn back the listeners from asking for the sending down of the angels. Thus Almighty God said: ﴿given respite﴾, meaning: granted a delay from the calamity We sent down upon them, by any one who grants delay for his own benefit, [what] lies beyond it, so that they might make up for some of what they neglected and consider something that concerns them. Rather, their seizing was, because of its ease for Us, in less time than a blink, and they could not defend themselves. So the punishment of this world befell them, and they passed on to the punishment of the Hereafter, so they lost both abodes, and they harmed no one but themselves.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 30:

Since the deliverance of the Children of Israel from the Copts was a remarkable matter, hardly believable, let alone that it would come about through the destruction of their enemies, Allah, glory be to Him, emphasized the report of this, pointing to the greatness that befits Him, as an alert that He is able to do the same for this Prophet (ﷺ) and his followers, even though the Quraysh deemed that impossible and thought themselves in their grip. So He said: ﴿And We had certainly delivered﴾, meaning: by what We possess of greatness, "a great deliverance," and although it was by means of separate signs that came about gradually, ﴿the Children of Israel﴾, Our devoted servants, ﴿from the humiliating punishment﴾, because they were among them in the category of slaves, employing men and women, and even more humiliating was the added control over the slaves through the slaughtering of their sons.

(p-32) When the listener was eager to know who the bearer of that punishment was, He said, substituting for what precedes it, to make it clear, since Pharaoh himself was a punishment because of his excessive harm to them: ﴿From Pharaoh﴾. Then He gave the reason for that, by what is known of him, the correctness of the description of him as a punishment, and He said, emphasizing, because the condition of Quraysh in oppressing the believers is the condition of one who denies that Allah saved the Children of Israel despite their weakness, so He will save others of the weak, or who denies that Pharaoh was powerful: ﴿Indeed he was haughty﴾, in his nature there was the deep-rootedness in exaltation, ﴿of the extravagant﴾, i.e., those firmly rooted in transgressing the limits.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 32:

When Quraysh took pride in the outward appearances of affairs, in adornment and deception, and regarded that as exaltation from Allah, and regarded weakness of condition in this world as misery and distance from Allah, He refuted their claim by pointing to what He did with the Children of Israel, despite their weakness and bad condition after the destruction of the family of Pharaoh with the punishment of annihilation. So He said, emphasizing against Quraysh's deeming it unlikely that One would choose those whose share of this world is small: ﴿And We chose them﴾, meaning: We acted, by virtue of the greatness We possess, in making them the chosen ones, in the manner of one who strives at that, and their matter became great, by His saying, building upon what its implied sense is: choosing (p-33) exalting [them] ﴿above knowledge﴾, meaning: from Us, regarding what would come from them of good and evil. It has become evident from its effects that you have come to ask them, while you are the plain offspring of Isma'il, peace be upon him, about what befalls you, and you make them your exemplars in what afflicts you, and you travel to them on the livers of camels. Thus, in a short time, everyone who follows your Messenger ﷺ, from among you and from among others, will become like this. When He had made clear the one preferred, He made clear the one over whom he was preferred, saying: ﴿above the worlds﴾, meaning: those existing in their time, through what We sent down to them of the Book and what We sent to them of the Messengers.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 33:

When He had informed them of their choice, He explained the effects of that choice, saying: ﴿And We gave them﴾, that is, in accordance with the greatness that is Ours, ﴿of the signs﴾, that is, the indications that point to Our greatness and to Our choosing them, from the time Musa, Our servant, peace be upon him, came to Fir'awn until he parted from them through death, and after his death through the hands of the prophets who affirmed his law, peace be upon them all, ﴿wherein there was a trial﴾, that is, a test of the kind that causes one who looks at it or hears it to incline, or to turn it away from what it was upon. This refers to the splitting of the sea, the shading of the cloud, the sending down of the manna and the quails, and other things they witnessed of the nine signs. In this there is also a deterrent for the Arabs from some of their sayings, out of fear of being snatched away by the Arabs and of poverty through the cutting off of trade from them, and other things. ﴿Clear﴾, that is, manifest in itself and making clear to others. How fitting this closing is to His saying at the beginning of their story: ﴿And We had already tried before them the people of Fir'awn﴾ [al-Dukhan: 17].

Now that it has been established by what has passed that He, glory be to Him, is characterized by giving life and causing death, and since denying this is obstinacy that no one who affirms God could deny, and since affirming it in some cases while denying it in others is arbitrariness that contradicts the judgment of reason and the decisive transmitted text, and since among the signs given to them was their being brought back to life after their death, when they asked to see God and the thunderbolt seized them, and when they left their homes, being thousands, fearing death, and that was indeed the Resurrection itself, while the Arabs denied it and exaggerated in their denial, and did not ask them about it, He said, rebuking them and indicating by emphasis that it is hardly to be believed that anyone would deny this given the proofs it has: ﴿Indeed﴾, and He belittled them by His saying: ﴿these﴾, meaning the lowly, the few, the humiliated, ﴿they say﴾, meaning: after the conclusive proof has been established against them, exaggerating in denial in contrast to the emphasis of affirmation:

"In" (إنْ), i.e., "mā" (meaning "not"). Since the Almighty's saying was previously mentioned: ﴿He gives life and causes death﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 8], and they knew that what is meant by it is that the giving of life is repeated for the one person, (p-35) and since He, exalted is He, had said, and He does not address them except with what they know: ﴿And you were dead, and He gave you life; then He will cause you to die, then give you life, then to Him you will be returned﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 28], meaning by dispersal after life, [and] He said: ﴿You made us dead twice and You gave us life twice﴾ [Ghafir: 11]. They said: ﴿It is not but our first death﴾, with the omission of a modifying noun (ḥadhf muḍāf, the dropping of a word understood from context); that is, "What is life but the life of our first death." ﴿The first﴾, meaning the one that was before the breathing of the spirit, as will come in Al-Jathiyah: ﴿It is not but our worldly life﴾. They described it as "the death" to indicate that life, beside eternal death according to their claim, is a thing that vanishes and has no proportion to it. And He, glorified is He, related their speech in this manner to indicate that matters, when the unseen is measured against the seen, the giving of life after "the second death" is more fitting, because it comes after a life, from the giving of life after the "first death." So He reduced the matter to the beginning having been from a death that was not preceded by life, and the settled state will be in a life that is not followed by death.

Since the meaning was: "And there is no life beyond it," they emphasized it with what makes it understood explicitly, so they said, rejecting what Allah had affirmed on the tongue of His Messenger, ṣallā Allāh ʿalayhi wa-sallam (ﷺ), (p-36) ﴿and we are not﴾, and they emphasized the negation, saying: ﴿resurrected﴾, meaning: from a dispersal by resurrection such that we would become beings of voluntary movement by which we disperse after death. It is said: "nashara-hu" and "anshara-hu," when he gives him life.

When they claimed that the assertion of resurrection could not be valid unless they witnessed one of the dead whom they knew alive again after his skin and bones had decayed, they, addressing the Prophet ﷺ and those who followed him, made their denial the basis (of their words): ﴿Then bring⦆ — that is, O you who claim that we will be raised after death — as a notice that they do not believe this, even though its adherents are many, from among their own kind and followers ﴿our fathers⦆ — that is, because we know them and know the abundance of their intellects, so we do not doubt [that] that is a revival of one who has died, so that it would be a sign for us of the resurrection. They reinforced their denial with His saying: ﴿if you are truthful⦆ — that is, if your truthfulness is established.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 37:

When they boasted of this greatness with excessive pride (tanaṭṭu'), since even if it were so, it would be no stronger proof of the establishment of prophethood, which entails the confirmation of everything the Messenger ﷺ says to them and brings them of signs, they were not fearful of Allah, though they knew His power and His destruction of those who came before them for denying the messengers, peace be upon them. It was as if they claimed a unique status in a position of power, in some respect or meaning, by which they might escape being made equal with those before them in that matter. So Allah, Exalted, said, rebuking them: ﴿Are they better﴾, that is, in religion and in worldly life, ﴿or the people of Tubba'﴾, that is, those over whom Tubba' ruled, spanning the earth in length and breadth, who founded al-Hira and built the palace of Samarqand. He was a believer, and his people were Himyar and those who followed them, the nearest of the destroyed peoples to the Quraysh in time and place. He had in Mecca the Honored what no one else had of monuments. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': he was the first to clothe the House (the Ka'bah), and he sacrificed six thousand camels at al-Shi'b, stayed there for six days, circumambulated the House and shaved his head. Al-Baghawi, after mentioning his story with the Ansar when his son was killed secretly in the Noble City (Madinah), and what the Jews admonished him with, to refrain from ruining Madinah because it is the place of emigration of a prophet [from] the Quraysh, said: he believed them and followed their religion, and that was before its abrogation. He said, on the authority of al-Raqqashi: Tubba' believed in the Prophet ﷺ seven hundred years before he was sent. And on the authority of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "Do not revile Tubba', for he was a righteous man."

Since this occurs in the context of the threat of destruction for their opposition, and since the destruction was only for some of those whose time had passed, not for all creation, he introduced the particle (preposition), saying: ﴿and those before them﴾, that is, [from] the famous affairs, such as Madyan, the People of the Thicket, the Rass, Thamud and 'Ad.

Since it was as if it were said: "What about these nations?", it was said: ﴿We destroyed them﴾, that is, by Our greatness, and even if they were great, these (Quraysh) do not perceive, in what power they have, that they cut off those whom Allah commanded be joined, of the messengers and their followers, and denied what they brought. For this reason, He gave the reason for the destruction as a warning to the Arabs, with His saying, emphasizing their assumption that their destruction would be merely by the custom of the age: ﴿Indeed, they were﴾, that is, by nature and disposition, ﴿criminals﴾, that is, deeply entrenched in wrongdoing. So let these beware, if they commit deeds like theirs, lest what befell them befall them as well.

When the purpose was to argue for the recompense, whose comprehensive principle is that it is fully administered on the Day of Resurrection, [the verse] "We did not create the human beings in vain, [so that] some of them would oppress others, and then they would not be held to account," was followed by something greater in appearance than it. So He said: ﴿And We did not create the heavens﴾, that is, despite their greatness, the vastness of each one of them, and their encompassing of what is beneath them. He used the plural because the more work increases, the further it is from being in vain. Moreover, perceiving their multiplicity requires observation, given what is in them of the stars. (p. 39) In Surah al-Anbiya', He used the singular, specifying what the deniers of resurrection can actually see, because of the restriction of "ladun" (ladun, a particle meaning "from the presence of") to what is hidden there, as was mentioned in that place.

Since the evidence for the correspondence of the lands was subtle, He used the singular for them and said: ﴿And the earth﴾, that is, together with what is in it of benefits, ﴿and what is between them﴾, that is, between the two kinds and between each one of them, [and what] is adjacent to it, ﴿in play﴾. That is, [the heavens and earth were created] with [a purpose consistent with] our greatness, which anyone with even minimal intellect perceives as exalted above play, because play is only done by one who is deficient. Had We left the people such that some of them oppress others, as you witness, and then We did not take from their strong ones on behalf of their weak ones what is rightly theirs, [creation] would have been play for them. Rather, play would be lighter than that. And in that hypothetical case, We would not deserve the attribute of holiness (al-qudduwsiyyah, the attribute of being utterly holy and pure from defect). For indeed: "A community is not sanctified in which the weak among them are not given their right from the strong among them without hesitation." This was narrated by Ibn Majah from Abu Sa'id, and by Ibn Jami' in his Mu'jam from Jabir, and by the author of al-Firdaws from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with them all, as a marfu' report (traced to the Prophet ﷺ). This is something that even the least of the rulers of this world would not accept for himself. Thus this was a decisive proof for the truth of the Resurrection, so that the separation through justice and grace would become manifest there.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 39:

When He negated that the creation of that (world) was a sport, which is vanity, He affirmed what He created it for, and He did not state explicitly what lies in between, because it is a consequence (tabi'), and what came before has already alerted to it (p-40). So He said, beginning a new sentence: ﴿We did not create them﴾, i.e., the heavens and the earth together with [what] is between them, ﴿except with truth﴾, that is, with the judgment (hukm) between those who are in them: [whoever] does vanity, We punish him, and whoever does truth, We reward him. By this there appears in the utmost clarity Our encompassing of all the attributes of perfection, as We alerted the people of perfection in this abode by creating them, whose actuality conforms to the truth, and that is what We have of those attributes that necessitate the Resurrection, to establish the truth and nullify falsehood, in a manner that is not hidden to anyone.

Since most of creation does not know this, due to its greatness, from reflecting upon its proof, even though it is definitive and self-evident:

﴿But most of them﴾, i.e., most of those among whom you are, who say: ﴿There is only our first death﴾ [al-Dukhan: 35], and likewise whoever goes in their direction, ﴿do not know﴾ [i.e.,] that We created creation for the sake of establishing the truth; so for that reason they become bold in sins and cause corruption on earth, not hoping for reward nor fearing punishment. Had they reflected upon what We fixed in their innate natures, they would have known with manifest knowledge that it is the truth from which there is no deviation, just as their rulers assume offices in order to make manifest judgment among their subjects, and stipulate judgment by the truth, and affirm upon themselves that they will not transgress it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 40:

Since it was as if it were said: "We see that most of the oppressed die in the bitterness of their choking grief, humiliated, and most of the oppressors depart triumphant in their aims, joyful, so when will this truth come?" He said, answering that, emphasizing it to refute their denial: ﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision﴾ (yawm al-fasl), at the gathering of the first and the last, from all the accountable beings, which everyone awaits, for the distinguishing between every mixture, so that it leaves no kind of it, to the point that it distinguishes between the hateful and the beloved, the abode of bliss and the cave of Hellfire, and between the people of each of the two by distinguishing the one who is right from the one who is false, through reward and punishment. It is after the resurrection (ba'th) from death. ﴿Their appointed time﴾ i.e., the time of gathering the creatures for judgment between them, which was set for them from eternity and which the Books were sent down with upon the tongues of the Messengers, ﴿all of them﴾, none of whom escapes it from among those who have died of the jinn, mankind, the angels, and all the animals.

When He mentioned this Day, whose greatness He indicated by this expression in its singular form and its construction, He mentioned of its description that which moves one to fear and hope. So He said, as a substitution from it: ﴿The Day when no master will avail a master﴾ in any way at all, ﴿a master﴾ by kinship or otherwise, by alliance or by bondage, from above or from below, ﴿anything﴾ of the availing that is intended to be taken from him for what he had done. And since availing sometimes occurs by gentleness and at other times (p-42) by force, He stated the second, because it is the greater of the two, and the context is one of destruction and subjugation, so He said: ﴿nor will they be helped﴾, i.e., the two categories, ﴿helped﴾, meaning by a helper such that, even if some of them wished to help others, or others wished to help them had it been supposed that they would help them. He expressed it in the plural, which the indefiniteness conveyed for "master," so that it would encompass the little and the much of it; for the negation of it is a negation of the individuals a fortiori.

When he had negated intercession, he made an exception to it, saying: ﴿Except for whom Allah has mercy upon﴾, meaning: the Supreme King wishes to honour them, and they are the believers, some of whom intercede for others by Allah's permission regarding the intercession for one of them. So He honours the intercessor concerning him by accepting his intercession, and He honours the one [interceded for] by accepting the intercession concerning him.

Since what preceded indicates the complete power over honouring and punishing, and honouring may come from weakness, He said, negating that and affirming the completeness of power, from which exclusivity in that is necessary, emphasising it, as an alert that this should not be placed before the eyes and have the fingers tied over it. Also, because their association of partners and their denial of the Resurrection includes denial of that: ﴿Indeed, He, He is the Almighty﴾, meaning: He alone is ﴿the Almighty﴾, the Invincible, whose might is not impaired by pardon or punishment; rather, that is a proof of His might, for He does what He wills to whom He wills, without concern for anyone.

Since the Almighty may not show mercy, He said: ﴿the Most Merciful﴾, meaning: whose might does not prevent Him from honouring (p-43) whomever He wills.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 43:

Since the context concerns retribution, he informs about the state of the wicked by way of resumption (isti'naf), and so he says, emphasizing what they deny: ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum﴾, whose description has already been given, in that it emerges from the root of the Hellfire and its spathes are like the heads of devils, and other things that no one knows in their true knowledge except Allah Most High. What you know of it in this world is that it is a tree with small leaves, pungent (dhafirah), meaning extremely foul-smelling, and bitter, derived from zaqm, meaning fierce gulping and excessive gorging. ʿAbd al-Haqq said in his book al-Wa'i: "Zaqqum is a dusty-coloured tree with small leaves, having no thorns, pungent (dhafirah), having knots (ka'abir) in its stalk, meaning joints like reeds, and it has a flower that bees gather from, and the top of its leaves is extremely ugly, and it is pasture, and its habitat is the plain." Ibn Burjan said: "It is in the Fire in opposition to the tree of Tuba in Paradise. They are compelled to eat it and to drink al-ghislin, just as the people of the world are compelled to force food into themselves."

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿The food of the sinner﴾ (ṭaʿām al-athīm)

That is: the one who goes to excess in acquiring sins, to the point that he has become accustomed to them, so that they have led him to disbelief.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 45:

﴿Like molten brass﴾ (al-muhl). That is: thin tar, and that which has melted of copper or iron, or its dregs. Aḥmad and al-Tirmidhī narrated it (al-Tirmidhī said: "We do not know it except through the hadith of Rishdīn"), and Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ, and al-Ḥākim by another route (al-Ḥākim said: "its isnād is ṣaḥīḥ"), from Abū Saʿīd (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His words ﴿Like molten brass﴾, said: 'Like the sediment of olive oil; when it is brought near his face, the skin of his face falls off into it.'" ﴿Boiling﴾ (taghlī), that is: the tree, according to the reading of the majority with the feminine form; and the food, according to the reading of Ibn Kathīr, Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, and Ruways from Yaʿqūb, with the masculine form. The pronoun does not refer back to al-muhl, because it is the thing used as a comparison (mushabbah bihi). ﴿In the bellies﴾, that is: from the intensity of the heat.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 46:

Since reminding people by means of what is known carries great weight in producing either attentiveness or aversion, even though it falls short of what it is compared to, He said: ﴿Like the boiling﴾, that is, like the boiling of ﴿the scalding water﴾, that is, the water whose heat has reached its extreme by what is kindled beneath it, so it bubbles up as though it wants to free itself from the heat it is in. Al-Tirmidhi (who said: "hasan sahih") related it, as did al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and al-Hakim (who said: "sahih according to the conditions of the two [Shaykhs]"), from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If a single drop of al-Zaqqum were to drip into the world, it would corrupt the livelihood of the people of the world, so what of the one whose food it is?"

Since it is as if it were said: "What is it with the sinner that he eats this food, and what drives him to it and to approaching its place?", it is answered that he is compelled to it, and that the attribute of might in Him requires mercy toward him by returning him, by saying to the angels of punishment: ﴿Seize him﴾, meaning, seize him by force, so do not let him have any control over his affair; ﴿then drag him﴾, meaning, drag him by force, with harshness, violence and haste, toward the torment and the humiliation, such that he is as if he were being carried. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': al-ʿatl (dragging) is to take hold of the collar of his garment at his chest and pull him. The reading with a ḍammah (ʿutlūhu) is more indicative of extreme harshness and severity than the reading with a kasrah (ʿitlūhu). ﴿into the midst of﴾, meaning, the middle of ﴿the Blazing Fire﴾, meaning, the fire in the utmost state of blazing and kindling, and it is the place from which the tree that is his food emerges.

When it had made this clear, [the sinner] came to be in a place where punishment surrounds him from all sides. He [Allah] made clear that he has another kind of distress, of a rank in greatness that deserves to be joined by the particle of delay (thumma), so He said: ﴿Then pour[1] over his head﴾, that is, in every direction which is "over his head," so that what is poured envelops his whole body, ﴿the torment of boiling water.﴾ That is, the torment with which the boiling water (ḥamīm) seethes, or which is itself the boiling water; and expressing it as "torment" is more terrifying. This stands in contrast to the blessing they had enjoyed through what descends from the sky, namely rain (p-46), so that the heat of the boiling water is gathered for them outwardly and the zaqqūm inwardly.

[1] Ṣubbū (صُبُّوا), from the verb ṣabba (صَبَّ), "to pour"; the doubled consonant indicates intensity or repetition of the action.

When this was known, that he has no power at all over his own affairs, but had reached the utmost degree of humiliation, He indicated it through mockery, in accordance with what he used to imagine within himself of the greatness by which he exalted himself in the world over the commands of God. So it is said, according to what its estimate implies, that He will do this to him, saying to him: ﴿Taste!﴾ That is: it is due to your deception toward the friends of God that this has brought you to it. And since the friends of God, from among the messengers and their followers, used to declare in the world that he, because of his refusal of God's command, is the humiliated one, and this sinner and his followers used to deny that and assert their saying which implies his greatness, in order to burn the hearts of the friends, He related to him their saying as they used to utter it, as an increase in his torment through rebuke and reproach, giving as the reason for the command to taste: ﴿Indeed you﴾, and He emphasized with His saying: ﴿you﴾ alone, apart from those who declare your lowliness, ﴿the Mighty﴾, that is, the one who overcomes and is not overcome, ﴿the Noble﴾, that is, the one who combines generosity with nobility of soul and greatness of disdain, so your concealing the evils of your character by displaying its virtues will not benefit you, for you are not ﴿base﴾, that is, stingy, humble of soul, and mean of disdain. So it is a metaphor for addressing him with baseness, together with establishing the proof of that through what he is in of ruin. And the reading of al-Kisa'i with the opening of "anna" indicates this punishment, in word and deed, according to what was said to him of this in the world while he himself believed it to be true.

When it had indicated that this is said to each of the sinners and that it is done to each of them individually, it indicated what they are being punished with. So He said, emphasizing it as a refutation of their denial, driving them toward a manner that conveys that it is the cause of what was mentioned of their punishment: ﴿Indeed, this﴾, that is, the punishment, in word, deed and state, ﴿is what you used to﴾, that is, by natural disposition and temperament, which We had made you to have, so that Our power might be manifest in your affair in this world and the next, ﴿doubt about﴾, that is, you used to trouble yourselves, compel your souls to doubt in it, and turn them back from the first natural disposition they have, which is affirming the possible, especially for one whose truthfulness has been tested and in whose hand extraordinary events of habit have appeared, to the extent that, because of the intensity of your rejection of him, you were as if you singled him out for doubt.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 51:

When He (subhanahu) had described what awaits the one who exceeds in evils, and had mentioned him first in the singular as an indication of the few in the people of this noble Prophet whom Allah rescued through his call, honoring him and elevating his rank, and then gathered them at the end, mentioning the traces of what made them deserve that, namely their sharing in his burdens, it was understood that the description of him had ended and passed away, so the soul yearned to learn what awaits their opposites, those who opposed him in his beginning and his return. He said, emphasizing what they had of denial: ﴿Indeed, the righteous﴾, i.e., (p-48) those who are distinguished in this description, ﴿will be in a station﴾, i.e., a place of residence in which the one who dwells there does not desire to move away from it, ﴿secure﴾, i.e., his companion is safe in it from everything that would displease him.

Since one description following another is especially effective in enticing toward something, He said, substituting for "maqam" (station): ﴿In gardens﴾, that is, orchards whose full description the intellects fall short of grasping, ﴿and springs﴾, likewise, such that the eyes are delighted by them.

When he had mentioned the description of what is for the inner self, the delight of looking and the clothing, food and drink, he followed it with the clothing of the outer self and what each has of nearness, and said: ﴿They will wear﴾.

When he had described what was prepared for them of clothing in Paradise, he indicated abundance greatly by his saying: ﴿of sundus (fine silk)﴾, which is the thinner silk made into garments of various kinds. He added another type, saying: ﴿and istabraq (brocade)﴾, which is the thicker silk made into linings, and it was so named for the intensity of its sheen.
