Since the description of the companions of the Fire was by what they have of being seized, each being preoccupied with himself and others, after what had preceded in Surat al-Zukhruf in the verse about the close friends, which made known that they would be turning their backs, he described their opposites by what they have of ease together with gathering, and said: ﴿facing one another﴾. That is, none of them turns his back on another, neither physically nor in meaning, and each desires that the other face him looking at him. [p-49] So when they desire women, the curtains come between them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 54:

Since this is a matter that dazzles the intellect, such that it can hardly be imagined, He said, emphasizing it: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning: the matter is as We have mentioned, equal, with no doubt about it. And since joy is not complete through it except by means of spouses, He said: ﴿And We will wed them﴾, meaning: We will pair them, as spouses are paired. The intended meaning is not the contract (ʿaqd), because it is a verb that is transitive by itself, and it does not occur in Paradise, since its benefit is lawfulness (ḥill), and Paradise is not an abode of obligation involving permission or prohibition. He mentioned the manifest form of greatness, as an alert to the completeness of nobility: ﴿with fair ones (ḥūr)﴾, meaning: [according to] the distribution, with bright, beautiful companions, pure of garments, ﴿with wide, lovely eyes (ʿīn)﴾, meaning: wide of eyes.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 55:

Since a person in this world fears the burden of expenses, He described what is there of abundance of good things, and said: ﴿They call for﴾, i.e., they demand, with a demand that is in the utmost of delight, ﴿therein for every kind of fruit﴾. No category is withheld from them, whether by distance of place, absence of season, or any other such matter. He said ﴿fruit﴾ to signal that, despite its abundance, it is not there for the establishment of proof, but is for enjoyment and mere pleasure. And since excess in pleasure is feared to lead to many dangers, He said ﴿secure﴾, i.e., while they are in the utmost security from every fearful thing.

(p-50) When He mentioned security, and since the thing that people of this world fear most is death, He said: ﴿They will not taste death therein﴾, meaning in Paradise, ﴿death﴾, meaning that the first beginnings of its tasting will not be renewed for them, so how much less what lies beyond that. Since the intended meaning is the negation of this in a way that yields certainty of safety in the highest degree, and since the *istithna'* (exception) is the measure of generality (*mi'yar al-'umum*), and since it is known that the tasting of death that occurred in this world, which is a meaning among meanings, has become impossible to recur, He said, giving the reason for and linking this impossibility: ﴿except the first death﴾. Since the meaning with the attribution of tasting to death is not ambiguous, because what precedes the breathing of the soul is not something tasted, He expressed it with His words ﴿the first﴾. The restriction by the adverbial phrase ("therein") makes clear that death is tasted in the Fire, and describing it as "the first" indicates that what is tasted is a second death. So it is as if it were said: "But those who are not God-fearing, who were disobedient and thus enter the Fire, will taste another death therein," as came in the sound hadiths. It is also permissible to make the description of the God-fearing more general, encompassing the firmly grounded and others, so that the judgment falls on the whole group, meaning that all of them do not taste it, while some of them, namely those disobedient ones whom God wills, taste it in another place, which is the Fire. It is also permissible that the first death occurred in a figurative Paradise, so that it is not a suspension upon something impossible. This is because the God-fearing person has always been (p-51) therein in this world figuratively, through what he causes for himself and through what God has previously decreed for him therein. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When a believer visits his brother, he remains in the harvest of Paradise until he returns." It was said: "What is the harvest of Paradise?" He said: "Its fruit." And: "When you pass by the gardens of Paradise, graze in them." Likewise, the one for whom a judgment has been made that he is therein, at the time of death and after it, through his enjoyment of looking and the like, and through eating for the martyrs and other things mentioned in the sound reports. Among that is what al-Bukhari narrated from Anas, may God be pleased with him, that his paternal uncle al-Nadr, may God be pleased with him, said on the day of Uhud: "O Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, the Garden, by the Lord of al-Nadr! I find its fragrance from beyond Uhud," and then he fought until he was killed. Then the completion of that bliss in Paradise occurs after the resurrection. Ibn Burjan said: "The world, when it is realized for the believing God-fearing person and he pursues contemplation of it, is a lesser Paradise, because of His, glory be to Him, taking charge of them in it, His nearness to them, His looking upon them, their remembrance of Him, their worship of Him, their preoccupation with Him, and He is with them wherever they are."

Since the context concerns the God-fearing, He said: ﴿And He protected them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾, meaning all the God-fearing, as a reward for what they guarded against, ﴿the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾, meaning the one whose burning of the sinner was previously mentioned. As for the disobedient who are not God-fearing, God admits into the Fire whomever He wills of them, and each of them is punished (p-52) according to the measure of his sins; then He causes them to die [therein], and they continue until God permits intercession for them, and He brings them out, then gives them life again by what the people of Paradise sprinkle upon them of the water of life. Imam Ahmad narrated in his *Musnad*, Muslim in the Book of Faith of his *Sahih*, Ibn Hibban in the Book of Intercession of his *Sunan*, and al-Darimi in the Book on the Description of Paradise and Hell of his *Sunan*, known as the *Musnad*, and Ibn Abi Hatim in his *Tafsir*, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "As for the people of the Fire, who are its people," and al-Darimi said: "who belong to the Fire," "they will not die therein nor live, but some people among you were touched by the Fire because of their sins," or he said: "because of their misdeeds, so God caused them to die a death." Imam Ahmad said: "So He causes them to die a death," and al-Darimi said: "The Fire afflicts them according to the measure of their sins, so they are burned therein until, when they become charcoal, He permits intercession, and they are brought." [And al-Darimi said]: "They come out of the Fire in clusters (*dabā'ir*), so they sprout upon the rivers of Paradise. Then it is said: 'O people of Paradise, pour upon them,' and they sprout." And al-Darimi said: "Their flesh sprouts like the seed in the flood debris." The *dabā'ir* (clusters): 'Abd al-Ghafir al-Farisi said in *Majma' al-Raghā'ib*: the plural of *dibāra*, like *'imāra*, is *'amā'ir*: groups of people. Abu Ya'la narrated from Anas, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Some people enter the Fire until they become charcoal, then they are admitted into Paradise. The people of Paradise say: 'Who are these?' It is said: 'These are the Jahannamites.'" And Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, [from the Prophet (ﷺ)], who said: "The Sirat is laid down," and he mentioned the intercession of the believers for their brothers after crossing the Sirat and God's permission [to them] to bring them out, [and he] said: "They bring them out of it and cast them into the water of life, and they sprout like the sprouting of seed in the flood debris." And Ibn Abi Umar narrated from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God will bring out a people from the Fire after they have been scorched therein and become charcoal. They will be cast into a river at the gate of Paradise called the River of Life, and they will sprout in it as the seed sprouts in the flood debris, or as the *tha'ārīr* sprout," and then they enter Paradise, and it is said: "These are the freed ones of the Most Merciful." *Tha'ārīr* (with the letter *tha'* marked by three dots, and *'ayn* and *rā'* unpointed): a plant like the *hilyūn*. At-Tirmidhi narrated, and said: "Hasan sahih," and it is narrated through various chains from Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: (p-54) "Some people of monotheism are punished in the Fire until they become cinders therein. Then mercy overtakes them, [and they come out], and they are cast at the gates of Paradise. The people of Paradise sprinkle water upon them, and they sprout as the scum grows in the carried flood, then they are admitted into Paradise."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 44, verse 57:

When the context concerns the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), it might be thought that what was done to them was a right owed to them, something unavoidable and inescapable. So He made clear that the matter is otherwise: that had He seized them (wa'akhadhahum) and not dealt with them by His grace and pardon, they would have perished. Thus He said: ﴿Grace﴾, meaning He did that for the sake of grace (fadl). For this reason He turned away from the mode of majesty (maẓhar al-'aẓama) and said, exalted is He: ﴿from your Lord﴾, meaning the One who is good to you (al-muhsin ilayka) through the perfection of His beneficence toward those who follow you, a beneficence befitting you. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': The root of faith is seeing grace in all circumstances.

When He magnified him (ﷺ) by making this attribute manifest and attributed it to him (ﷺ), He increased his exaltation by indicating it with the demonstrative of distance, saying: ﴿That﴾, meaning the great, wide grace, ﴿is indeed﴾ [i.e., exclusively] ﴿the triumph﴾, meaning the attainment of all objectives, ﴿the great﴾ one, which left no station of nobility unfilled.

(p-55) When He, glory be to Him, presented in this surah what the Qur'an possesses of blessing, through what it contains of good tidings and warning, of gathering and distinguishing, and reminded them of what they acknowledge, that He is the Originator of this universe, which necessitates their affirmation of His Oneness, which in turn entails that He does whatever He wills, such as sending and sending down, admonishing and resurrecting, and other things, and threatened them with what no one but Him can bring about, namely the smoke and the mighty seizing, and did some of that, and reminded them of what they know of the reports of those who passed before, the leaders of earlier generations, and that despite all of this they denied the resurrection, then mentioned what calls for warning and good news, all of this in methods that reached every goal and rendered all powers incapable, along with the dazzling meanings and the brilliant, overpowering stylistic beauties it contains, He then gave as a causal result, as a recapitulation (fadhlakah) of the surah, His words: ﴿So We have only made it easy﴾, i.e., We have made it a great ease and a considerable facility.

When a person's eloquence increases and his rhetoric becomes greater, his speech becomes clearer, his words sweeter, firmer, more fluent and more solid. The Prophet (ﷺ) was the most eloquent of people and the furthest of them from affectation for this reason, so He attributed it to him alone and said: ﴿in your tongue﴾, i.e., this clear Arabic, and they are Arabs who are impressed by eloquence, ﴿that perhaps they may remember﴾, i.e., so that they would be, in the presence of one who sees them and knows their language, one whose state is like theirs, in hope that they might remember (p-56) that this Qur'an is evidence, by its inimitability, of the soundness of what it contains of Oneness, messengership and other matters that have come to you and been made manifest to you. Otherwise they, being the most eloquent of people, would have been able to oppose any part of it, so that they would remember what they had neglected: that He is All-Mighty, by destroying the tyrants, and that He is All-Wise, by setting up signs for His prophets and supporting them with miracles; and that a great man among them does not accept that anyone should attack his greatness, nor that one under his authority and subjugation should oppress others, and then not help the oppressed against his oppressor and take his hand, so that the doer of good is not treated equally with the doer of evil. So when they remember that, along with what they know of the power, majesty and wisdom of the King, they will know with certainty that there must be a resurrection to distinguish between the people of righteousness and corruption, and to separate all the servants. Consequently, His words follow: ﴿So wait﴾ [al-Dukhan: 59], i.e., wait for what I have hoped for you from their remembrance, which entails their guidance.

When they were showing defiant arrogance and obstinacy, claiming that they did not care at all about the Qur'an or anything else that he brings, and did not count any part of it as a sign, He informed about what they conceal of their fear and their waiting for everything with which he threatens them. He emphasized it for the sake of those who took their arrogance to be true steadfastness, so He said: ﴿Indeed they﴾, and He increased the matter by informing with the noun that indicates permanence and continuity, so He said: ﴿are awaiting﴾. That is, their imposing upon themselves watchfulness and their exertion of thought in that is constant; it does not leave them, rather it has cut through their hearts and filled their breasts. Thus the end of the surah corresponds to its beginning, and even to the intended meaning of its general and detailed themes, by mentioning the Book and the awaiting of various kinds of punishment. And Allah is the Guide to what is correct, He is the Generous, the Bestower.
